newsitem.title: LEBANON: Unlicensed Lebanon media get new lease on life.
newsitem.headline: Unlicensed Lebanon media get new lease on life.

text.p: Lebanese Information Minister Bassem al-Sabaa said on Saturday that scores of unlicensed private television and radio stations in Lebanon would not have to shut down by midnight as ordered to do earlier.

Sabaa told reporters that a media law, under which most of the 200 or so private stations operating in the country were to close by midnight November 30, would be "implemented under a new mechanism to be studied...in the few coming days."

The government has licensed only 15 private television and radio stations. They include four television stations, three of which are owned or controlled by establishment figures like billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri.

Opposition groups and media workers have complained that the authorities were deliberately attempting to muzzle the media by refusing to grant licences to all opposition television and radio stations, including some of Lebanon's most successful.
They also said that the decision to give licences only to stations linked to officials amounts to a carve-up of the broadcasting industry.
Sabaa did not specify the grace period given to the stations but some Beirut newspapers said on Saturday that the cabinet would meet soon to decide on the issue.
They said the grace period may be for one month, during which applications by some of the unlicensed stations would be studied to decide if they would get licences.
However, a standing ban forbidding the unlicensed stations from broadcasting news or political programmes would continue during this period, they added.
